title: Obliques
summary: The muscles on the sides of the trunk: the external and internal obliques, plus the serratus anterior along the ribs under the armpit, which the app shows in the same region. They rotate and side-bend the trunk, resist twisting, and (serratus) move the shoulder blade forward.

what_it_is.overview: In the app the obliques region is the external obliques and serratus, from the outer edge of the six-pack to the side of the torso. The internal obliques sit underneath and work with them.

heads.name: External obliques
heads.origin: The outer surfaces of the lower eight ribs.
heads.insertion: The front half of the pelvic rim and a broad sheet that meets the six-pack in the midline.
heads.fiber_direction: Run down and forward, like hands in front pockets.

heads.name: Internal obliques
heads.origin: The lower-back fascia, the pelvic rim and the groin ligament.
heads.insertion: The lower ribs and the midline sheet.
heads.fiber_direction: Run up and forward, at right angles to the external obliques.

heads.name: Serratus anterior
heads.origin: The outer surfaces of the upper eight or nine ribs, in finger-like slips.
heads.insertion: The inner edge of the shoulder blade, on its rib-facing side.
heads.fiber_direction: Wrap around the ribcage from the front to the shoulder blade.

what_it_does.action: Trunk rotation (the external oblique on one side works with the internal oblique on the other).
what_it_does.detail: The job in woodchops and landmine rotations.

what_it_does.action: Side bending, and resisting side bending and twisting.
what_it_does.detail: Why suitcase carries and Pallof presses train them.

what_it_does.action: Help flex the spine and brace the trunk.
what_it_does.detail: Why crunches and leg raises credit them a little.

what_it_does.action: Pulls the shoulder blade forward around the ribs and rotates it upward.
what_it_does.detail: Active at the top of push-ups, in punches and when reaching overhead.

synergists.name: Abs
synergists.role: Flex and brace the trunk with the obliques.

synergists.name: Quadratus lumborum
synergists.role: Side-bends the trunk from the back; not tracked.

synergists.name: Upper and lower traps (for the serratus)
synergists.role: Rotate the shoulder blade upward together.

antagonists.name: Opposite-side obliques
antagonists.role: Rotate and side-bend the other way.

stabilizer_roles.text: In one-arm carries and presses the obliques resist side bending; suitcase carries are rated 0.8.

relationships.indirect_note: Each working set adds the exercise's rating for this muscle to the weekly total, and ratings under 0.25 count as 0. 3 sets of cable woodchop (1.0), 2 sets of suitcase carry (0.8) and 3 sets of hanging leg raise (0.5) give 3 + 1.6 + 1.5 = 6.1, which the panel shows as 6 (rounded to the nearest 0.5). The full list comes live from exercises.json; the rows above are examples and the ratings are coaching estimates.

how.joint_angle: Turn the trunk against a cable or landmine, with the hips mostly still.
how.grip: Two hands on a handle or bar end.
how.stance: Standing side-on, feet about shoulder width.

bias.caveat: Rotation machines make loading easy and stable.

how.joint_angle: Hold the trunk still while a load tries to twist or tip it.

bias.caveat: Isometric work; progress by load or time.

how.joint_angle: Push the shoulder blades forward at the end of a press or push-up.

bias.caveat: The library has no dedicated serratus exercise and does not credit push-ups to obliques; any serratus work there is a model.

best_exercises.why: Loadable rotation with cable tension; obliques 1.0.

mistakes.text: Turning the hips with the shoulders so the trunk barely rotates.
Leaning toward the weight on suitcase carries.

coach_cues.cue: Turn from the ribs, hips quiet.
Stand tall; don't lean toward the weight.
coach_cues.why: Makes the carry an anti-side-bend drill.

coach_cues.cue: Press out and hold; don't let the handle pull you round.

notes: Weekly target in the app: 2 to 12 obliques sets at Advanced. Intermediate and Beginner scale the minimum by 0.8 and 0.6; the maximum stays the same. Render the numbers from targets.json, not from this text.
No oblique or serratus growth study by exercise choice is on file, so nothing here is marked supported.
Targets are low and marked extrapolated; most people get oblique work from carries, leg raises and rollouts.
